newsitem.title: UK: UK adviser says demand growing too rapidly.
newsitem.headline: UK adviser says demand growing too rapidly.

text.p: Gavyn Davies, a member of the UK Treasury's panel of independent economic advisers, said demand was growing at a "rapid and probably dangerous" rate and policy should therefore be tightened.
"Demand is now growing too rapidly," he told the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee.

"We're getting lots of information from the monetary indicators and the labour market indicators and the survey indicators that demand may grow very rapidly next year, more rapidly than the Treasury is forecasting."
Davies said the budget was not very restrictive in its impact on demand.
"The implication of my...remarks is that interest rates have to go up further," he said. "I am unpersuaded that the performance of sterling should be used as a reason for not raising interest rates."
Davies said base rates needed to rise to 7.0 percent by the middle of next year to ensure the inflation target would be hit in 1998. Base rates currently stand at 6.0 percent.
The government has set itself a target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation.
